text: We ripped up the rulebook. No beige tablecloths. Just the topmost quality beans. No chit-chat. No pretense. It doesn't matter if you are just getting acquainted or have it down to fine art. Coffee's here for you to enjoy. Plus company of those who roasted it for you.
about.title: What is roast!?

colab.description: Roast! would be nothing without the participation of roasters, exhibitors, speakers and sponsors. If you fall into this category, be sure to click to find out more.

sponsors.text: Are you a company that likes to support community events? You can be rewarded with a logo on the event, promotional materials, tickets and interesting packages for your employees.
sponsors.title: Sponsors

colab.title: Let's join forces!

exhibitors.text: Information for exhibitors, participating roasters, cafes and coffee equipment dealers.
exhibitors.title: Roasters and presenters

101.annotation: At 101.ROASTERY, we believe that good coffee tastes great anytime, anywhere. That's why we carefully select the best beans, roast them with the utmost precision, and fine-tune every step to ensure that the resulting flavor is always perfect. Whether you enjoy your coffee with us or at home, you can be sure that it's just right. ☕

baristaroasters.annotation: We are a small roastery from southern Slovakia. We have been roasting select coffee for 6 years. We strive to find the most interesting coffees, whether in terms of their story or flavor profile, so that they are memorable and provide an experience.

black.annotation: Specialty coffee is a product we have trusted since our beginnings in 2017. We started with a small espresso bar but our curiosity took us further. Today we are a local roaster from Bratislava with global ambitions. We are building a brand that is worth following for its uncompromising commitment to unique varieties, interesting flavours and innovative roasting style. Because although we are black. we're constantly striving to make every day a little brighter and more special.

coffeespot.annotation: We are a select roastery from Babice. Since 2011, we have been selecting and roasting only the best beans for you, so that you can feel that we have put everything into our coffee from the very first sip, and bid it a bittersweet farewell with the last. We enjoy what we do and who makes up our roastery. Thanks to this, we have a really close relationship both here among ourselves and with our suppliers from all over the world. And over the years, we dare say that we have the same relationship with our customers. We roast small batches every day to ensure that our coffee is always fresh. Nothing leaves our doors that we haven't tasted and approved.

annotation: Coffee Culture, an Ostrava-based coffee project run by two enthusiasts of the world of specialty coffee. Our goal is to bring specialty coffee to the widest possible audience.
We regularly focus on fresh coffee harvests from around the world. The key for us is to recognize the maximum potential of each one and then bring it out to the fullest during roasting.

Our customers are cafés and enthusiasts who already know their way around specialty coffee, but also cafés that want to improve their output. We help them with both education and technical support. Many of them have found their niche in a professional approach to barista work and the diverse flavors of specialty Arabica coffees.

For 80 years our family business has grown and distributed the finest Colombian coffee to local exporters. In 2015 we expanded our operations and began producing, sourcing and exporting speciality coffee to the rest of the world.

As growers, we specialise in alternative fermentation processes that are new to Colombia. On our farm and in our Processing Centre La Pradera, the most exotic varieties are processed achieving unique profiles that are unknown for Colombian coffees.

Cofinet also represents and supports a large number of Colombian Specialty coffee growers. Our aim is to encourage direct relationships between our farmers at origin and roasters around the world. We pride ourselves on creating sustainable, ethical and long-term relationships

We have established a strong relationship with a group of high-quality associations from Peru, who share our sustainability and traceability values. These associations work with farmers whose love and commitment to coffee are reflected in every single lot they produce. We must say that we have been stunned by the cup potential of Peruvian coffees.

One of our aims is to source the best coffee from Peru, but what really drives us is being able to work with the local community and have an impact in both social and economic ways. Our processing team provides continuous guidance to several smallholders in three different regions around Peru in order to improve the cup quality and achieve alternative profiles, never seen before in Peru. The results so far have been super promising and we cannot wait to share these coffees with you. We strongly believe that working hand in hand with growers is the only way to produce outstanding coffees.

chcikofein.annotation: We are Miro and Maru – husband and wife, coffee addicts, and a little bit crazy, roasting coffee for like-minded enthusiasts. We roast in a one-kilogram roaster because we like to experiment, and a smaller roaster allows us to do that. It also means we can change our range more often, and from time to time you will find some real limited editions.

dalia.annotation: A roastery from Silůvky near Brno, we roast excellent select coffee on a modern Coffee Crafters hot-air roaster. Come and taste both classic and experimental coffees at our brew bar.

annotation: Dos Mundos is a coffee roaster based in Prague. Our coffee is the result of meticulous work and a passion for discovering new flavours that reflect the unique character of each coffee region. We work directly with farmers to ensure fair conditions and promote sustainable coffee growing practices.

In addition to selling coffee, we also focus on spreading coffee culture through workshops, tastings and educational programs. Dos Mundos is a place where tradition meets innovation and where passion for coffee is transformed into a real experience.
Knock, knock... Who's there? Francine Roasters! Who? Just good coffee!
They have caffeine in their blood and a roaster as their weapon. Their mission? To roast a selection and deliver a coffee that makes you go, "Mmmm, this is how it's supposed to be".

Filtered with a hint of fruit? Espresso that tastes like a chocolate dream? František and Olda, our main roasters, always have an answer. It's also because we support small farmers. We buy coffee directly from them, so every bean has a story and we know what we're offering.

We also like to experiment - we have a coffee for the hipster and your grandmother because we believe everyone deserves the perfect cup. And most importantly, we're no quick-fixes - we roast with love and care because we know where we're coming from and where we're going.

We're pretty wide ranging with over 30 varieties of coffee from all over the world, so there's something for everyone. In addition, we have two cafés of our own - Go Francin in Smíchov and Kafe Fracin in Letná - and we are working on another one.
Because we have something for everyone, we even have capsules packed with the best selection.

We can proudly say that in Libeň, where we roast our pedigree coffees every day, it smells like heaven on earth - and when you add our humour to the mix, it's clear that this coffee is not made by a boring corporation.

gills.annotation: We are one of the oldest and friendliest coffee roasters in the center of Brno, run by Marek and Martin. Over the years, we have figured out what we want, and now we are bringing it to you at the festival.

hayb.annotation: Hi, How Are You Brewing? We're HAYB - speciality coffee roasters based in Warsaw, Poland. We like fun processings, risky bean experiments, but we also enjoy the stable quality of ordinary daily brews - both the funky and the classic ones. We want those beans to bring some colour to your cup - every day and on special occasions. We roast with the deepest respect for the origin. No compromise on taste. No compromise on quality. This job drives us energetically not only due to caffeine. All done for you to deal with your coffee with ease and joy, having fun with various possibilities that good coffee can give you. Effortlessly!

annotation: We do what we love. Coffee.
We are a newly opened roastery that focuses on quality, taste and culture. Coffee beans from different parts of the world are roasted to bring out their potential and flavor.
The variety in coffee offerings ensures that you will always make the right choice when selecting your coffee.

We are a young roastery with a selection of coffees located near Brno, in Hradčany near Tišnov. We carefully select coffee beans from different parts of the world to bring you coffee that offers a unique taste experience.
Each batch is roasted with love and care because we believe that coffee should be an experience.
IG Coffee Roasters - these are select coffees where every bean has its own origin and story.
As our valued partners and sponsors, you'll find IG at their own booth on both Saturday and Sunday! 🖤

Our name is Kmen. That means "the Tribe" in czech, it has deep roots and gives rise to new branches. Petr, our head roaster, brought fine coffee to South Bohemia eight years ago with his then roastery Fragaria Coffee and has a long history behind the bar at Café Datel. It was there that his collaboration with Lucia and Kryštof, who are involved in running the roastery and espresso bar, began. We've all been working with choice coffee for a long time, but together everything is new for us: new name, new people, new space and new packaging too

We don't believe in one right taste, every crop, every field is different and tastes different. Whether we were in Panama or Peru, we were secretly eating ripe coffee cherries on the farms. There, you realise that coffee is actually a fruit. And this is what we want to say with our packaging and everything - coffee does not have one universally correct taste, quite the opposite. So on every bag you will find the fruit (admittedly, sometimes it will be nuts, chocolate or gummy bears) that is most characteristic of the coffee.
There, on a hill in Lhota overlooking the surroundings, where the farmers used to store their tools and grain on the cuttings, stands OUR KOLNA - the Czech artisan coffee roasting shop.

We are a family-run roastery just outside Benesov and thanks to our many years of experience and knowledge of coffee we can offer you coffee of the highest quality. We offer coffees for lovers of bitter and chocolate flavours, as well as for coffee enthusiasts who enjoy fruity (yes sour) flavours and interesting processing methods.

labanda.annotation: La Banda Caffeina – a caffeine cartel for everyone who isn't afraid of strong flavors and even stronger decisions. Each bean is the result of a secret operation between fire and time, creating a pure taste and aroma that will put you in a trance. Join our gang and drink coffee without compromise forever.

liskafe.annotation: We have been operating since 2022 and we are probably one of the smallest roasters in Brno. We work only with a selection of coffees and we are currently most interested in fermented and fruit-infused coffees, which is why you will find several of them in our offer. And since we roast in small volumes and try to change our coffee portfolio often, almost everything is a bit of a limit. If you'd like to taste our coffee, drop by the Mug café, which is at the end of the 12 bus in Brno.

lot.annotation: We are Lot – a coffee roastery from Bratislava, where we believe that great coffee is no accident. Every step, from selecting the beans to roasting, is done with the aim of capturing the true flavor and character of coffee. If you're looking for pink, you'll find us. See you in Brno!

mamacoffee.annotation: At mamacoffee, we combine the highest quality coffee with fair and sustainable trading. We focus on working directly with the farmers to deliver not only a great cup of coffee, but also the unique stories behind it. You can buy coffee and much more from our e-shop or from one of the 7 cafes we operate in Prague. Where, in addition to delicious coffee, you can also enjoy pastries from our own artisan bakery.

annotation: Welcome to The Miners! We are a specialty coffee roaster and a growing network of cafes proudly operating in the Czech Republic and Spain.

At The Miners, we believe that great coffee starts at the source. That's why we work exclusively with specialty coffee, proudly sourcing beans directly from the most respected farmers around the world. We carefully roast beans from 13 different countries, using special roasting methods that highlight the unique flavors of each origin. Our dedicated team is committed to thorough research and relationship building to ensure that every cup you enjoy is the epitome of quality and honest craftsmanship.

We understand that exceptional coffee deserves exceptional baristas. That's why we've created a comprehensive weekly training course that prepares our baristas to make you the perfect cup every time. The training culminates in an exam that ensures our baristas have all the necessary knowledge and skills.

We believe in excellence in everything we do, and our commitment to quality is reflected in every carefully roasted bean. We use modern, cutting-edge technology such as La Marzocco and Slayer coffee machines to ensure that every cup is prepared with the utmost precision and care.

At The Miners, we are driven by a passion for sourcing the best beans from the best farmers around the world. Our team works hard to build strong relationships with these dedicated growers who share our unwavering commitment to world-class excellence.

parabellum.annotation: Para Bellum Lounge is an establishment combining quality hookahs and a modern bar in the very centre of Brno. It is an ideal place for a friendly board game session, a quiet home office with fast internet, or a date with a tasty drink and an excellent pipe. You can find us near Malinovsky Square at Sukova 4.

penerini.annotation: We are Petr, Nela, Rita and Nikola, a family that loves coffee. At the family table, the idea of quality coffee for home users, coffee enthusiasts, baristas and coffee drinkers was born, and from it came the roastery Penerini coffee. We are creating a coffee culture across the Czech Republic through courses and participation in events, and festivals. We surround ourselves with people who crave perfect flavours as much as we do and sell what we love most.

pikola.annotation: We are Pikola. At the foot of the Jeseníky Mountains we roast the finest coffee with respect for its origin. We are constantly on the lookout for exceptional coffees that stand out from the norm in terms of aroma and taste. Thanks to long-term relationships with our suppliers and farmers, our roastery offers you fresh coffees from this year's harvest. Our offerings are changing, but the freshness and quality remain. We do everything with respect and love for nature.

annotation: We were born as a Punkt café. in the first specialty coffee wave, like a little Berlin on Bayerova Street in Brno. With the arrival of the new branch on Štefánikova Street, we gradually started to build a roastery. At both spots you can taste our daily production, which we regularly supplement with funky limits in our offer. Slowly but surely, we are succeeding in getting our coffee beyond our premises into homes and businesses
We'll see you at the festival on Saturday at the espresso bar and Sunday at the brew bar. We look forward to seeing you there.

quickborn.annotation: Quickborn Roastery is a specialty coffee roastery that brings a unique experience directly to you, wherever you are. With our stylish horsebox and portable bars, we can create an authentic coffee atmosphere in the most unusual places.

mala_prazarna.annotation: We re a small coffee roastery located in the heard of Ljubljana, Slovenia. Our happy place is next to our local coffee community. Finding the best coffees we can, gives us the biggest high. It will be our first time in Brno and we cant wait ti meet you all

ohmybean.annotation: We are Oh My Bean, and we have dedicated our lives to coffee. We roast it for our own cafés and dozens of others in Czechia and abroad, we take care of your caffeine supplies at home or at work, and above all, we are here for you so that you don't get lost in the world of coffee. We advise, explain, and show you. We believe that choosing, preparing, and drinking good coffee is not just for the chosen few, but for everyone.

rebelbean.annotation: Rebelbean is a roaster of specialty coffee, it also is their own network of cafes and most importantly it's an energy for everyone who is not afraid to be a Rebel and go for their ideas and dreams. We live and do business in Brno and we are happy to be able to supply energy to this festival.

wildkaffee.annotation: Wildkaffee is a specialty coffee roastery based in Farchant, near Garmisch-Partenkirchen in Germany. Established in 2010 by Stefanie and Leonhard Wild, the company is guided by four core principles: quality, innovation, transparency and sustainability. Each roast is a considered expression of these values, a reflection of thoughtful sourcing, precise technique and a deep respect for the art of coffee. With bases in Austria and Thailand, and a growing presence around the globe, Wildkaffee coffees are enjoyed by discerning partners and coffee lovers worldwide.

red_fawn.annotation: We are Red Fawn from Trnava – two brothers who love specialty coffee. We roast sweet and juicy coffees that don't taste like a compromise. Fresh harvests, pure taste full of fruit and character. Come and taste the experience, not just caffeine.

trafficcoffee.annotation: We are Traffic Coffee – a roastery from Olomouc, where we create select coffee with character. We roast traditional beans as well as bold experiments such as barrel-aged coffee from aromatic alcohol barrels. Both coffee conservatives and adventurers will find something to their liking here.

tripple_five.annotation: We are a specialty coffee roaster in Bratislava. We carefully select the highest quality varieties from different corners of the world. Through careful roasting, we strive to bring out the full flavor that each bean has to offer.

the_roses.annotation: A family business run by brothers Vojtěch and Matyáš Růžička together with their father Oldřich. Since 2017, they have been focusing on specialty coffee with an emphasis on quality, fair trade, and sustainability. We purchase coffee directly from producers around the world, operate cafés, a training center for baristas, and a roastery.

ws_home.name: How NOT to make a filter
ws_home.annotation: Taste and see how poor filter preparation affects the flavor. We will answer the question of why we prepare drip coffee within certain parameters and put into context the variables that affect the flavor of coffee, whether positively or negatively.

ws_sensory.name: Sensory training - supercharge your senses
ws_sensory.annotation: We see with our eyes and taste with our whole body. This workshop will focus on sensory perception and teach you how to perceive taste, smell, and touch more accurately—and how to connect your senses into a single whole. You will discover that even ordinary water can have dozens of flavor nuances and that sensory perception is not the preserve of sommeliers or baristas, but of each and every one of us. Through practical training, you will open the door to a deeper understanding not only of coffee, but also of food, wine, and life itself.

ws_yerba.name: After this Yerba Maté workshop, you'll stop drinking coffee
ws_yerba.annotation: Discover why Yerba Maté is conquering the world as a healthier alternative to coffee. This workshop will reveal why Yerba Maté surpasses coffee in terms of energy, concentration, and lifestyle. Come and taste the change directly from the founder of the largest Yerba Maté brand in Czechia and Slovakia. You will learn how to prepare Yerba and how to benefit from it in the long term.

ws_water.name: Water – more important than coffee itself
ws_water.annotation: Let's take a closer look at water. Although it is not widely known, water is more important than anything else when it comes to making coffee. Have you ever wondered why the filter coffee tasted great at the café, but the same beans suddenly didn't taste as good at home? Here's the answer.

ws_whisky.name: The story of whiskey
ws_whisky.annotation: The story of whisky's journey from barrel to glass. The workshop will also include whisky tasting by Tomáš Dyntar and pairing with specialty coffee.

ws_cupping_penerini.annotation: Come and taste coffee from the Peneriny roastery. Cupping is lead by the Peneriny roastery staff.

ws_cupping_traffic.annotation: Come and taste coffee from the Traffic Coffee roastery. Cupping is lead by the Traffic Coffee roastery staff.

ws_roasting.name: Roast your own beans
ws_roasting.annotation: Every roaster has, in addition to their beloved large roaster, a small test roaster. This is used to roast samples from importers and farmers. During the workshop, you will learn how to work with such a small roaster. You will receive a few dozen grams of coffee of your choice, which you can roast and take home with you.

ws_esko.name: Your own espresso
ws_esko.annotation: In two consecutive workshops (Espresso and Latte Art), we will look at the basics of preparing specialty coffee. How to set up the grinder correctly, why we use scales, and how to prepare milk for latte art correctly.

ws_qb.name: Cupping uncensored
ws_qb.annotation: Discover how coffee tastes when you remove all filters. At the workshop, you will learn the basic rules of cupping—a professional method of coffee tasting that reveals its aromas, flavors, and flaws. Together, we will go through the entire process step by step. At the end, you will taste unusual coffees—Arabica, Canephora, and rare Liberica.

ws_choco.name: Discover the beauty and diversity of chocolate
ws_choco.annotation: Did you know that high-quality chocolate can be very similar to high-quality coffee? In this workshop, you will learn about the history of chocolate, how it is made, and the different types available. All this will be accompanied by a guided tasting.

ws_kaple.name: Tasting and wine sensory analysis
ws_kaple.annotation: Something like cupping, but in the world of wine. Join us as we take a look at the forms of tasting and identifying wine defects.

ws_hradsky.name: Dripper Showdown
ws_hradsky.annotation: At a time when a new dripper for preparing filtered coffee is created every week, it is not easy to navigate the range on offer. In this workshop, you will prepare coffee together using five different drippers and have the opportunity to compare how each one affects the taste, aroma, and overall character of the cup. You will see for yourself how small differences between drippers can change the resulting coffee experience, and you may discover which dripper is right for you.

ws_latte.name: Your own cappuccino
ws_latte.annotation: In two consecutive workshops (Espresso and Latte Art), we will look at the basics of preparing specialty coffee. How to set up the grinder correctly, why we use scales, and how to prepare milk for latte art correctly.

ws_cupping_chicas.annotation: Produkční cupping pod vedením farmářky Angely Rojas. Ochutnáte experimentální zpracování a speciální loty, které se normálně ani neimportují do Evropy.

ws_cupping_lot.annotation: Come and taste coffee from the LOT roastery. Cupping is lead by the LOT roastery staff.

ws_cupping_punkt.annotation: Come and taste coffee from the Punkt roastery. Cupping is lead by the Punkt roastery staff.

talk_arana.name: The Real Price of an Exotic Lot
talk_arana.annotation: An exotic lot can land in your roastery at a price that raises eyebrows, but almost nobody in the chain can tell you where that money actually goes. In this talk we follow one real Colombian lot from the farm to a European warehouse — what the producer earns, what the processing costs, and what gets added by milling, shipping, customs and storage. Having gone from a cupping table in Valle del Cauca to the buying side in Europe, I've seen how differently each end describes the same coffee. You'll leave with a clearer picture of what you're paying for, and five questions worth asking your importer before your next purchase.
talk_arana.bio: Santiago Arana grew up in Sevilla, a coffee town in Valle del Cauca, and started out at the local growers' cooperative, cupping coffees from more than three hundred producers in the region. He joined Cofinet as a sales rep and is now Commercial Manager for Cofinet Europe, working with roasters in over forty countries. His job, the way he sees it, is simple: getting the people who grow the coffee and the people who roast it onto the same table.

talk_biology.name: Coffee for everyone (even children?)!
talk_biology.annotation: We all love coffee, but what does caffeine do to our bodies? And what happens when caffeine is consumed by children? Pediatrician Dr. Barbara Šťastná will talk about how much caffeine adults and children consume today and what it does to us.
talk_biology.bio: Medical doctor Barbara Šťastná, a pediatrician working for Jihomoravské dětské léčebny (South Moravian children's sanatories). Among other things, Barbara is a trainer at the Loono organization, a fencer and archer at a summer camp for children, and an amateur tailor.

talk_green.name: Seven burning questions about green coffee
talk_green.annotation: Importer Tereza from Chicas Industry covers seven of the hottest topics in the world of green coffee—and devotes exactly seven minutes to each one. From the difference between fermentation and infusion, to the myth of the "poor farmer", to the question of whether we are asking too much of coffee. Fast-paced, sharp points, and seven different perspectives that may change your view of the coffee world.
talk_green.bio: I am a mom, entrepreneur, lover of foreign cultures and languages, and formerly a frequent traveler. I have been involved with coffee since 2011, and with specialty coffee since 2014. Since 2019, together with my colleague Karolína, I have been developing the Chicas Industry project focused on importing green coffee.

talk_humberto.name: Celebrating Coffee's Transformative Power
talk_humberto.annotation: We will discuss the impact of coffee and how it can transform people's lives across the entire supply chain. This includes its effects at origin, as well as the roles of importers, roasters, baristas, and guests.
talk_humberto.bio: Humberto Ribes, a Spanish barista living in Berlin. Currently Head of Coffee at the Five Elephant roastery in Berlin. Among other things, Humberto is a talented photographer.

talk_ks.name: Coffee journalism on the rise
talk_ks.subheading: The editorial team of Káva spojuje
talk_ks.annotation: How do you write about coffee and gastronomy in a way that readers will enjoy? The editors of Káva spojuje magazine will openly reveal everything that goes on "behind the keyboard" – from finding topics to behind-the-scenes interviews to what never makes it past the editors' scrutiny. Come take a peek into the editorial kitchen and ask anything you want to know about journalism.
talk_ks.bio: We believe that "coffee connects". We are an online editorial team that aims to become a trusted voice connecting the coffee community across the Czech Republic.

talk_helena.name: Coffee quality from farm to cup
talk_helena.annotation: What goes into turning a coffee bean into a aromatic cup on your table? Helena Oliviero from Italy's SCA will guide you through the journey of coffee, from cultivation on plantations, through harvesting and processing, to roasting and preparation. You will learn how each step affects the final taste and why quality is not created in the cup, but long before that.
talk_helena.bio: Helena Oliviero is a multiple winner of coffee competitions, a Q-Grader, and an experienced trainer who discovered her passion for coffee while working part-time in Tuscany. After years spent in various European countries, she has become a respected expert and inspiration for baristas and coffee lovers around the world. In her work, she also addresses the issue of gender inequality in the coffee industry and encourages women to have the courage to change stereotypes.

talk_alice.name: Bean There, Roast That, Roasting through play, myths, and alchemy
talk_alice.annotation: Just pour in the green beans, turn on the roaster, and you're a roaster, right? Basically, yes. In this lecture, we will show that coffee roasting is not just about "feeling", but about consistency, data, and understanding the processes. We will break down the basics and add tips on how to approach roasting with perspective and ease.
talk_alice.bio: A coffee professional with more than 15 years of experience in gastronomy. Alice comes from Slovakia but has also lived in Greece and Germany for some time. She is currently the head roaster at the Rebelbean roastery in Brno. She also coached two-time Czech Barista Championship winner Denis Kramář.

talk_tanzanie.name: Coffee in Africa - how to do business in Africa
talk_tanzanie.annotation: He escaped from computers, spreadsheets, and figures straight to Africa. Ladislav Kolář from Jindřichův Hradec turned his life upside down and went from being a successful financier and co-owner of a brokerage company to a coffee grower. In Tanzania, he manages his own coffee plantation covering almost 30 hectares, provides jobs for local people, and also supports schools.
talk_tanzanie.bio: The Kolář family from Kolda Coffee. Owners of a 28-hectare plantation in the Mbeya region of Tanzania, they planted their first tree in 2012 and harvested their first coffee beans in 2016. Today, they have 86,000 trees on their farm, support sustainable agriculture, keep bees, build water retention areas, and work with the local community.

talk_madalin.name: About competitions
talk_madalin.annotation: About the course and participation in Austrian coffee competitions and the WBC in Milan. Just a week before the Roast! Festival, the Austria Coffee Championship takes place. How did the competition go? We will find out from the Austrian Barista of the Year 2020, Madalin Truica.
talk_madalin.bio: Madalin Truica, a coffee professional working as Head Barista at The Pelican Coffee Company in Vienna. He was born in Romania but grew up in Germany and has been involved in the coffee community for at least 10 years. In 2020, he won the Austria Barista Championship.

talk_tripplesenzory.name: Sensory battle – what do wine, beer, and coffee have in common?
talk_tripplesenzory.annotation: What do good wine, decent beer, and specialty coffee have in common? And how do their worlds differ? A brewer, winemaker, and roaster will share their experiences with the sensory properties of these three traditional beverages and show that the world of flavors is much more diverse than you might think.
talk_tripplesenzory.bio: The panel discussion will feature Michaela Neméthová, "beer doctor", certified BJCP judge, and brewer. Also participating will be Jiří Vyzourek, whose great passion is natural wines, which he deals with professionally at the Kaple wine bar in Brno. Last but not least, they will be joined by Jan Židů, roaster and owner of the Au Lait espresso bar in Brno, who will take care of "the coffee part".

talk_influencers.name: Like, share, drink – gastroinfluencing on social media
talk_influencers.annotation: Instagram, TikTok, YouTube – where does food taste best today? Three different food influencers reveal how food and drink are presented on social media, what is just a well-arranged illusion, and what is genuine passion. A discussion about authenticity and creative content.
talk_influencers.bio: Well-known Brno Instagram reporter Pavel Černý will meet with his "colleagues in the field", coffee YouTuber and podcaster Tomáš Taussig and gastro-freelancer and social media manager Petra Vlková.

annotation: ...songs about things that might have happened to you

A band from the independent Brno scene whose original music draws on indie rock, jazz, world music, grunge, and swing. Upon closer inspection, the entertaining Czech lyrics also conceal darker themes and leave the listener with the feeling that the world is a place full of love and indescribable horrors.
Honza Sysel (guitar, vocals), Libor Třeška (trumpet, guitar, vocals). Terka Volmutová (bass, vocals), Vašek Hadrava (drums)
Achievements, awards:
2nd place at Porta 2025
Selected by the City of Brno to perform at the 2025 Christmas Markets
Participation in the Slunovrat 2026 festival – Welcome Kofola Stage, among 10 selected bands out of a total of 133 applicants.

party_topol.annotation: Topol and Holič is a collaboration between musicians from Brno who, driven by their shared passion and friendship, blend songs with electronic music.

party_fanglou.annotation: Fanglou is a Brno-based band that blends jazz, funky groove, pop, and rock energy. They describe themselves as part of the so-called “Brno pop” genre! The band consists of Jiří Wolf on drums, Jiří Tůma on percussion, Pavel Kocián on bass, Josef Mucha on guitar, Jan Wolf on keyboards, and Jiří Slatina on vocals.

party_jan_vana.annotation: Jan Váňa is a singer-songwriter and lyricist originally from Tábor in South Bohemia. He usually performs with an electric guitar and a bass guitar, looping both instruments through a computer, but lately he has been preferring the acoustic guitar on its own. He has released two self-recorded EPs and several singles; in 2021, he performed as part of the Wombat Sessions series, and in May 2021, he released his first studio double single, titled "Tajem", written in collaboration with Prokop Korbe (aka badfocus). He also invited Korb to produce his debut album, "A na Jordán dopadla tma", which was released in April 2024. He currently lives in Prague, where he studies songwriting and screenwriting at the Jaroslav Ježek Conservatory. This is reflected in his music, where lyrics play a very important role.

bracia.annotation: Bracia Ziolkowscy means Ziolkowski Brothers. It's a speciality coffee roastery run by - surprise, surprise - two brothers. The elder is a neat Mr President in a tie. The younger is a slightly dishevelled activist in flannel. Polish Roasting Championship 2nd place in 2025 and 3rd in 2021.

cafe_cult.annotation: Importer of Cult Café coffee, accessories and equipment for coffee preparation.

annotation: The Hrnček Roastery was founded in 2026 through the merger of the family-run Liškafé project and the Hrnček community café located at the tram terminal in Brno's Komárov district.
We've been working with specialty coffee for 4 years now, and this year we've once again prepared some real coffee gems for you.

mia_coffee.annotation: A family roastery from northern Bohemia. We offer great coffee, delicious teas, and equipment for home or gastro use.

coffee_banditos.annotation: Coffee Banditos isn't just about coffee. It's about the experience, the passion, and a community of people who love great coffee just as much as we do. Coffee Banditos — because coffee should have character.

annotation: “We are a small family-run roastery in Kroměříž that was founded over a cup of specialty coffee in August 2013.

Our vision is to provide coffee of the highest quality and exceptional flavor. We source green coffee beans from trusted suppliers from around the world and devote the utmost care and attention to every detail during the roasting process.

The roastery's founding was preceded by a two-year period of learning, testing, and searching for the ideal method of roasting and brewing coffee. As a result, today we focus primarily on specialty single-origin coffee, but we also offer carefully crafted blends to suit various taste preferences.
For lovers of high-quality coffee and a healthy lifestyle, we also offer decaffeinated coffee that retains its full flavor, aroma, and character even after gentle processing.
We pride ourselves on freshness and quality at every step. After roasting, coffee needs time to 'rest' - usually 2 to 3 days - during which its flavor notes and aroma fully develop.

zoban.annotation: ZOBAN — a roastery from Litoměřice focused on specialty coffee with SCA scores above 85. We roast with respect for every bean. Proof? A silver medal at the Global Coffee Awards Europe 2025. Simply specialty coffee for discerning palates.

kikafe.annotation: We believe in naturalness, attention to detail, and moments that don't need to be rushed. Wherever you enjoy our coffee, we're glad it becomes part of your everyday little moments of comfort.

annotation: We are coffee holists. We roast coffee, brew coffee, drink coffee. We care about everything - from bean quality and origin to fair treatment of farmers, coffee technology, and barista craft. We believe this approach delivers the best taste in every cup you try with us.
From our first roasting experiments over 10 years ago, we've grown into our current qb coffee roasters with an espresso bar in Brno.
We are Kopi Bean, a Brno-based roastery where coffee is always a story, never just an anonymous bag. We carefully select every coffee, communicating with suppliers and growers from around the world.

Before beans reach our large IMF air-flow roaster, we fine-tune every profile on Ikawa and Roest sample roasters. We care about the details, because details make the difference between good and great coffee.
Come taste what we're roasting at Roast 2026!

beberry.annotation: At Be Berry, we see coffee as a form of art. Every roast is an adventure that brings new, unforgettable tones of flavour and aroma into life. Discover the extraordinary in every cup - because Be Berry is coffee for those who aren't afraid to explore.

poppy.annotation: Poppy Beans is a Brno-based specialty coffee roastery and Czech Coffee Roasting Champion 2024. It focuses on carefully selected coffees with transparent origins and roasting that lets the natural character, sweetness, and complexity of every bean shine through.

prazirna_krok.annotation: Pražírna krok was born in the heart of Jičín as a natural continuation of our café Všehochuť. Since 2024, we've been roasting specialty coffee right across the street, proving that even a small town can have a roastery with big ambitions. Every cup is an honest step forward — for us and for Jičín.

jungle_roastery.annotation: Jungle Roastery is a small craft coffee roastery that combines a passion for specialty beans and exotic flavours. It focuses on freshness, sustainable farming, and direct contact with growers. Every cup offers a unique profile, full of wild tones and the unmistakable atmosphere of the jungle.

la_boheme.annotation: La Bohème Café has been among the pioneers of specialty coffee in the Czech Republic. Since 2003, we've been sourcing coffee directly from farmers around the world and roasting it with respect for its origin. We build on quality, long-term relationships, and the belief that behind every cup there's a story worth knowing.

annotation: We are Stop.Time, a Slovak-Czech funk-rock band from Brno. We mostly play original music with drums, guitar, bass, saxophone, and keys.
"Everything is in 4/4 if you count long enough."

party_jazz_damu.annotation: The Brno-based band Jazz Baía mainly plays classic swing tunes, jazz standards, and Brazilian bossa nova. But you'll also hear their own takes on hits by Nirvana and Michael Jackson.

annotation: Vážky is a group of musicians who love life and liveness! Almost all members have a formal music education.
The band is made up of solo players who enjoy each other's company, go on trips together, play in pubs, and that's why they occasionally meet on a shared stage to share the joy of playing together.

party_druha_kapelka.annotation: From quiet melodic moments to monumental walls of sound. A four-piece from Brno rooted in alternative rock with shoegaze elements and a wide palette of other influences. The band prides itself on Czech lyrics with themes of melancholy and music with a feel for atmosphere.

annotation: Founded in 2010, Five Elephant is dedicated to setting the highest standards in specialty coffee. With a focus on sustainable sourcing, ethical practices, and meticulous roasting, we collaborate with producers who are committed to environmental regeneration and exceptional quality.
From our single-origin coffees to the Meridian collection, we celebrate the diversity of terroirs and varietals that honor the legacy of generations past and those yet to come.
Thoughtful choices shape every step we take.

ws_espresso_tonic.name: Espresso & Tonic Tasting – It's all about the tonic!
ws_espresso_tonic.annotation: Espressotonic, Eskotonik, E&T – or whatever you want to call it. This trend of hot summer days is firmly established on the menus of virtually every specialty coffee shop. And the tonic matters – in most cases, tonic makes up more than 70 per cent of the drink, and as lovers of cocktail drinks know, every tonic tastes different. Led by Karolína Lužová, you'll get to taste nearly a dozen different tonics – both premium and standard varieties – combined with two types of espresso.
ws_espresso_tonic.bio: Hi, I'm Kája, and I've been working in a café for several years now. Coffee has gone from being just a drink to something I'm increasingly enjoying discovering. I'm always up for a good filter coffee, and my guilty pleasure is fermented coffee.

ws_ice_filter.name: Ice Ice ~~Baby~~ Filter – Tasting preparations of cold filters
ws_ice_filter.annotation: Ice drip, cold brew, chilled brew, batch over ice – it's hard to keep track of them all. A tasting workshop where you'll sample a whole range of different ways to prepare cold filter coffee, all using a single variety of coffee. Each has its own characteristics, and every result is slightly different. Let's sort out the terminology once and for all, and perhaps even work out which method is best.
ws_ice_filter.bio: Hi, I'm Kája, and I've been working in a café for several years now. Coffee has gone from being just a drink to something I'm increasingly enjoying discovering. I'm always up for a good filter coffee, and my guilty pleasure is fermented coffee.

ws_gongfu.name: The Gongfu Cha tea ceremony
ws_gongfu.annotation: The workshop will feature a demonstration of the traditional gong fu cha tea ceremony and explain the significance behind the names of different types of tea. The workshop will focus on four types of tea: white, green, oolong and black.
bio: I served for two years in the elected role of tea master at the Klub Čajovna student club. I regularly organised tea tastings for both club members and guests.
The club itself is one of the finest venues for tea culture in the Czech Republic, where we regularly invite experts and organise tea workshops.

ws_grandma.name: Speciality coffee just like Grandma used to make (Melitta, Lamka and Karlsbad-style coffee maker vs. V60)
annotation: What might a speciality coffee prepared by a grandmother using the equipment available in the past have tasted like?

You won't find a Melitta, a Lamk or Karlovy Vary cutlery in cafés any more. Is that a shame, or is it actually a good thing? During the workshop, you'll taste one coffee prepared in four different ways – three traditional and one modern. The question is: can old-school coffee equipment still hold its own against the widespread V60?
ws_grandma.bio: We're Miro and Maru from the Brno-based micro-roastery Chci kofein. We're a married couple, coffee addicts and a bit mad, who roast speciality coffee for like-minded madcaps.

ws_milk.name: Milk under the microscope - Sensory characteristics and their impact on the flavour of coffee
ws_milk.annotation: Milk is often an overlooked ingredient in coffee, yet it can radically transform its flavour. During the workshop, we will taste various types of milk – from commercial and UHT varieties through to farm-fresh and competition-grade – both on their own and in combination with a single shot of espresso. Together, we will observe how the sweetness, texture, aroma and overall flavour profile change.
ws_milk.bio: Patrik Sláma has long been involved in coffee education and has been working as a coffee trainer for several years. He focuses primarily on sensory evaluation, coffee preparation, milk and latte art. In recent years, he has also been working on a book dedicated to the sensory evaluation, physics and chemistry of milk microfoam and latte art. As well as training, he is also involved in coffee journalism as editor-in-chief of Káva spojuje and Okafi magazine.

ws_beer_sensory.name: Beer Sensory Analysis, or "Why Does My Beer Taste Like Coffee?"
annotation: Imagine a perfect world where we strive to achieve a high degree of efficiency. That's why we'll all drink the same beverage—a blend of coffee and beer. Why should we like it?
Or, let's talk about the basics of beer sensory evaluation and whether there's a reason to infuse beers with coffee extract.
bio: Miša was practically a lifelong student (Food Technology), but is now a successful "Beer Doctor" who is somewhat known to the public as the "Evil Brewer" for her herbal beers, as well as a judge and co-organizer of beer competitions. She has over 5 years of experience in brewing in various countries, including the Czech Republic, Cyprus, and Estonia...
Currently, she manages production at a small brewery while also serving as the brewmaster. If you meet her, you'll likely witness an unintentional stand-up comedy/tragedy.

ws_naked_espresso.name: Better Vessel - The Hidden Flavor of Espresso
ws_naked_espresso.annotation: Espresso was born out of a desire for speed. From Angelo Moriondo's 1884 patent through the first commercial machines by Luigi Bezzera and Desiderio Pavoni after 1901, coffee was brewed using steam pressure—and had no crema. That didn't appear until 1948, when Achille Gaggia replaced steam with a lever-operated piston and a pressure of around nine bars. The thick foam, which no one expected, was quickly touted by marketers of the time as proof of quality. Since then, both baristas and customers have taken it for granted as an integral part of the cup. Better Vessel, a device from the Philippines by Michael Harris and Federico Bolaños, challenges this assumption. Revolution, evolution, or nonsense? Try it, and you'll understand :)
ws_naked_espresso.bio: The story of Jakub Fiala and coffee began in 2005, when he first visited coffee plantations during business trips to Indonesia to source wood. His visits to the plantations and processing facilities captivated him so much that in 2007 he began roasting coffee imported from small-scale farmers himself. Today, he is the driving force behind the Brno-based brand Kopi Bean, where he roasts carefully selected specialty coffees on a modern Italian IMF roasting machine. He approaches espresso the same way he approaches roasting profiles—there's always room for improvement.

ws_latteart_poppy.name: Pour your heart out: Latte art with Terka
ws_latteart_poppy.annotation: How do you create a heart, a tulip or something a bit more daring out of milk? Terka will guide you through the basics of latte art and show you how to work with the milk, the jug and the cup itself. You'll try out the free-pour and etching techniques and discover that there's no magic behind a successful design – just the right technique, a bit of patience and plenty of milk. And most importantly – don't worry if your first attempt ends up looking like a swan.
ws_latteart_poppy.bio: Terka works as a barista at Poppy Beans café in Brno, where latte art is her daily passion. She enjoys both free-pour and etching, and when she's not creating designs in cups at work or at home, you might spot her at one of the latte art competitions, where she regularly makes it through to the final. Now she's keen to share her experience and know-how with you too.

talk_coufalova.name: The hidden science in a cup: How microorganisms shape the flavour of coffee
talk_coufalova.annotation: Why do some coffees taste of jasmine and citrus, others of ripe blueberries, and still others of tropical fruit or rum? The key lies in what happens to the coffee cherry long before it is roasted. Take a look at the world of coffee through the lens of microbiology. We'll explore the journey from traditional processing methods to modern controlled anaerobic fermentation. We'll explain clearly and accessibly how yeasts and bacteria build flavour precursors in the bean, what the real difference is between co-fermentation with fruit and artificial infusion, and what a fascinating role biochemistry plays in the whole process.
talk_coufalova.bio: Ing. Mgr. Martina Coufalová, microbiologist. Fascinated by the role of fermentation in various aspects of human life, she decided to broaden her education to include food technology. Thanks to this, she can help you explore coffee from the perspective of the biochemical processes and microbial fermentation that fundamentally shape its final flavour profile.

talk_podcast_ect.name: Podcast LIVE: Where is the European coffee scene heading?
talk_podcast_ect.annotation: European Coffee Trip began as a blog and guide to cafés. Today, it has become one of the most prominent platforms on the European coffee scene. How has the world of speciality coffee changed over the past twelve years, how can you spot a really good café, and what do the data from thousands of establishments reveal about European coffee culture? Patrik Sláma will be discussing all this in a live podcast with Aleš Pospíšil, co-founder of European Coffee Trip.
bio: Aleš Pospíšil is the co-founder and CEO of European Coffee Trip, a platform connecting speciality coffee lovers with cafés across Europe. He founded the project in 2014 together with Radek Nožička, and they have gradually built the original café guide into an international coffee media outlet and community.

Patrik Sláma is editor-in-chief of the editorial team at Káva spojuje and Okafi magazine. He specialises in coffee journalism, content creation and coffee education. He connects the coffee community through interviews, articles, podcasts and other formats.

talk_kocar.name: Coffee shot!
annotation: Every café, product or member of staff deserves to be shown in the best possible light! Let's go through a few tips, insights and pieces of advice together on how best to film and photograph your business or your favourite coffee. The workshop is designed for both those with their own cameras and those who film on their phones. And you'll most likely find the insights you gain here useful even beyond the realms that smell of coffee.
The only photo and video workshop in the Czech Republic tailored to all café-goers – this really won't just be a slide show.
talk_kocar.bio: An internationally active filmmaker. Former lecturer in video at Masaryk University. Founder of the audiovisual production company KoPro. Someone who has finally learnt how to water his plants.

talk_blahovec.name: The creation of the book Kávový Baťa
talk_blahovec.annotation: A discussion on how the book Kávový Baťa came about. Hubert Lamplota – a name that, over 100 years ago in Czechoslovakia, was legendary in the world of coffee.
talk_blahovec.bio: Boris Blahovec is a coffee enthusiast, amateur historian, traveller and writer who has long been dedicated to the history of coffee and coffee culture. Through his collection of historical coffee makers, he enjoys bringing to life forgotten stories linked to coffee. At the talk, he will discuss the creation of his book Kávový Baťa and the story of Hubert Lamplot, a prominent figure in Brno's coffee scene. He will also share interesting facts from his historical research and the world of coffee.

talk_ajala.name: Hot Chocolate: Where It All Started
talk_ajala.annotation: Did you know that for most of its history, chocolate was consumed primarily in liquid form? The fascinating evolution of this ingredient includes many surprising and entertaining moments. During this lecture, we’ll introduce the “bean-to-bar” concept as a return to traditional methods and explain how this approach shapes the final flavor profile. We’ll also go over the practical details of preparation—from the ideal temperature to the importance of aeration for the full development of flavor. We’ll then connect theory with practice during a tasting, where you can explore these nuances with your own taste buds.
talk_ajala.bio: Emma, who is in charge of training, sensory workshops, and quality control at the Ajala chocolate factory in Brno, will guide you through the lecture and tasting. She is one of the few experts in the Czech Republic certified by the prestigious British institute IICCT (Level 1 & 2 Certificate in Chocolate Tasting). She passionately introduces the public to the complex world of cacao and delights in inspiring a deeper understanding of honest and ethically produced chocolate.

talk_chickas.name: A New Chapter for Chicas Industry: Specialty Coffee from the Forests of Indonesia
talk_chickas.annotation: This lecture will offer a brief insight into the work of a specialty coffee importer and introduce Indonesia as Chicas Industry’s new project. Although this country has been intriguing us for nearly two years, we are only now preparing to go there and are beginning to build relationships with local producers. However, thanks to our collaboration with BOKU University in Vienna, we’ve already had the opportunity to learn about a number of projects from afar that stand out not only for the quality of their coffee but also for their commitment to the environment, local communities, and sustainable development. We’ll share what we love about Indonesia and which farmers and projects we’d like to introduce to roasters and coffee lovers in the Czech Republic and beyond.
talk_chickas.bio: Karolína Nekvindová and Tereza Prejdová are the founders of Chicas Industry, a company that imports premium green coffee from Colombia, Mexico, Indonesia, and India. They have been involved in the coffee industry for many years and share a passion for its diversity, origins, and the stories of the people who grow it. In their work, they connect farmers with roasters and build relationships based on long-term collaboration, transparency, and mutual respect.

talk_angela_chickas.name: More than just a process: how exceptional coffee is made
talk_angela_chickas.annotation: A presentation by Angela Rojas from Colombia, co-founder of the Quebraditas Coffee Farm project, will tell the story of the farm and its journey towards an experimental approach to coffee processing. She will demonstrate that, although the chosen processes are a key part of the final quality, it all begins with the plant itself – the variety, the roots, the soil, the nutrition and the ripeness of the coffee cherries. Using specific experiments and two processes from the farm as examples – washed Geisha with thermal shock and SL28 Advanced Natural – Angela will explain how decisions made from cultivation right through to processing influence the final flavour of the coffee in the cup.
bio: Angela Rojas is a Colombian coffee producer and co-founder of the Quebraditas Coffee Farm project in the Huila region.
She became involved in coffee after returning to her home region during the Covid pandemic, when she and Edinson Argote began working on the family farms.
Within the project, she is primarily responsible for administration, agronomy and soil management.
Together with Edinson, she combines traditional cultivation with experimental coffee processing methods.
Their approach is based on soil health, plant care and a long-term quest to find ways to improve the quality of the coffee.

talk_gloria.name: Not all coffee is the same!
annotation: How does a lifelong passion for bartending give rise to a successful liqueur brand? This talk will take you behind the scenes of the founding and development of Gloria Spirits, which since

We’ll explore the entire journey – from the initial idea and bartending experience, through the development and production of premium coffee liqueurs, to building the brand on the domestic market. We’ll take an in-depth look at the specifics of working with coffee in liqueur production, where the discovery of new profiles and processing techniques never ends.

At the same time, we’ll gain an insight into the world of community events and bartending competitions that have sprung up around Gloria. We’ll introduce the Gloria Challenge concept and its links to the prestigious Coffee in Good Spirits competition, which bridges the precise world of coffee culture with modern mixology. Come and hear a story of courage, craftsmanship, coffee and entrepreneurship in the Czech gastronomy scene – without rose-tinted glasses.
bio: Honza has been involved in the Czech and international gastronomy scene for 16 years. Behind the bar, he has worked his way through every stage of the trade, which naturally led him to develop a deeper passion for coffee – a field he has been dedicated to for a long time and in which the discovery of new flavours, profiles and processing methods is a never-ending journey for him.

Since 2023, he has channelled this passion as co-owner and creator of the emerging Czech brand Gloria Spirits. He is behind the development of the premium coffee liqueur Gloria Single Origin and the innovative ready-to-serve cocktail Gloria Negroni. In his work, he combines the honest craft of bartending, a meticulous approach to coffee and a desire to take the Czech distilling craft to the next level.

talk_sloficek.name: Coffee and a nap
talk_sloficek.annotation: Coffee and a nap – two little pleasures that compete with each other in the world of sleep. Let's find out just how complex the process of sleep actually is, and how coffee can disrupt it. Does that one cup of coffee really not affect your sleep? And is an afternoon nap a way to refresh yourself, or rather a tried-and-tested way to ruin your night's sleep? So have a coffee, listen to the talk, and hopefully you won't fall asleep during it :)
talk_sloficek.bio: Barbara Šťastná, M.D. is a paediatrician with experience working in both general paediatric practices and specialist clinics focusing on childhood obesity and cerebral palsy. She loves coffee (especially filter coffee with a good bit of acidity) and perhaps loves sleep even more. This year, she will combine both in the topic of her talk. In her spare time, she dances, travels a lot, sews her own clothes or gets buried in a book.

talk_pranachai.name: Prana Chai - No Powders, no syrups
talk_pranachai.annotation: A chai latte that matches the quality of specialty coffee.  This is what Prana Chai set out to do when they started tinkering and brewing their handmade sticky chai in the back of a small coffee shop kitchen in Melbourne, Australia, 17 years ago.  We will explore why it came about, what it’s made of and how to prepare it.
talk_pranachai.bio: Matthew is the sales manager for Prana Chai in Czech Republic.  He joined the Prana team after working 14 years in hospitality.

text: We are a group of Brno coffee enthusiasts and professionals who decided to bring the culture of European coffee festivals to Brno.
You can meet individual members of our team behind the bar in several Brno cafes, roasters, bars and other establishments.
What binds us together is our love for specialty coffee and gastronomy.

content.title: Unlimited coffee consumption
content.text: With the price of admission, you can sample coffees from all the roasters present throughout the festival.

content.title: Lectures
content.text: You can expect lectures from well-known café owners, coffee roasters and other personalities from the industry. Take the unique opportunity to meet those who make it possible for you to enjoy the finest coffee. Admission to the lectures is included in the price of admission.

content.title: Workshops
content.text: Try out different coffee brewing methods or roast your own coffee. Capacity of the workshops is limited, so come early. Participation in the workshops is included in the price of admission.

content.title: Cuppings
content.text: Are you curious about how the taste descriptions of individual coffees are created? Come and taste coffee as it is tasted and evaluated by professionals. Participation is included in the price of admission.

content.title: Cups and mugs
content.text: For each participant there is a reusable coffee and beer cups available and ready to be borrowed. A deposit is paid on site. And of course there is also a cup rinse available free of charge for everyone so we all can enjoy each coffee from a clean cup.

content.title: Chill-out zone
content.text: If you want to relax during the festival, we have a relaxation area with deck chairs and seating.

content.title: Snack bar
content.text: Tasting coffee for two days in a row is not easy, that's why we also offer other snacks of all kinds. Beer, lemonade, coffee-based and other cocktails, salty and sweet food, hookahs... Whatever you can think of.

content.title: Specialty coffee to buy
content.text: Love what you're tasting? You can buy beans directly from the roasters during their presentations! If you missed your favorite coffee while it was on the grinder, don't worry—you can find a selection from our exhibiting roasters at the central festival booth all weekend long.

content.title: Festival merchandise
content.text: As well as coffee, we also have various other coffee products available for purchase. Plus, special Roast! Festival merch.
